questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The least area of a circle circumscribing any right-angle triangle of area $\dfrac{9}{\pi} sq units is$
questions.solution:
Let the sides of the right-angled triangle be $a$, $b$, and $c$, where $c$ is the hypotenuse. The area of the triangle is given by $A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab = \dfrac{9}{\pi}$.

The radius $R$ of the circumcircle of a right-angled triangle is half the length of the hypotenuse, so $R = \dfrac{c}{2}$.

By the Pythagorean theorem, $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$. Since $a^2 + b^2 \ge 2ab$, we have $c^2 \ge 2ab$.

Substituting $ab = 2A = \dfrac{18}{\pi}$, we get $c^2 \ge 2 \times \dfrac{18}{\pi} = \dfrac{36}{\pi}$.

The radius $R$ satisfies $R^2 = \dfrac{c^2}{4} \ge \dfrac{36}{4\pi} = \dfrac{9}{\pi}$.

The area of the circumcircle is $S = \pi R^2$.

Since $R^2 \ge \dfrac{9}{\pi}$, the minimum area is $S = \pi \times \dfrac{9}{\pi} = 9$ sq units.

Answer: 9 sq units

questions.q: $A B C$ is a triangle with $\angle A=30^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $B C=10 \mathrm{ cm}$. The area of the circum circle of the triangle is
questions.solution:
\bar{Z}=-1-i We know that,
$\angle B O C=2 \angle B A C=2 \times 30^{{}^{\circ}}=60^{{}^{\circ}}$ Since, $O B=O C\therefore \angle O B C=\angle O C B=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^{{}^{\circ}}-\angle B O C\right)=60^{{}^{\circ}}$
So, $\triangle B O C$ is an equilateral triangle.
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad O B=B C=10 \mathrm{ cm} \\ \text{ Therefore, area$ of $circumcircle } &=\pi(O B)^{2}=\pi(10)^{2} \\ &=100 \pi \mathrm{sq} \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: T. The angles $A, B$ and $C$ of a $\triangle A B C$ are in A.P. If $b: c=\sqrt{3}: \sqrt{2}$, then the angle $A$ is
questions.solution:
It is given that $A, B, C$ are in $\mathrm{AP}$. Now, $\quad A+B+C=180^{{}^{\circ}}\Rightarrow \quad B+2 B=180^{{}^{\circ}}\Rightarrow \quad B=60^{{}^{\circ}}$

Now, using sine rule, we have $\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}\Rightarrow \quad \sin C=\frac{c}{b} \sin B=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \times \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}} \quad[\because b: c=\sqrt{3}: \sqrt{2}]=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\therefore \quad c=45^{{}^{\circ}}$ Now, $\quad A+B+C=180^{{}^{\circ}}\Rightarrow \quad A+60^{{}^{\circ}}+45^{{}^{\circ}}=180^{{}^{\circ}}\Rightarrow \quad A=75^{{}^{\circ}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sides of a triangle are $x=2, y+1=0$ and $x+2 y=4$. Its circumcentre is
questions.solution:
The vertices are $(2,-1),(6,-1),(2,1)$ forming a right angled triangle. Circumcentre is the mid-point of the hypotenuse,

i.e., $\quad\left(\frac{6+2}{2}, \frac{1-1}{2}\right)=(4,0)$

questions.q: If the angles of a triangle are in the ratio $3: 4: 5$, then the sides are in the ratio
questions.solution:
Let the angles of triangle are $3 \theta, 4 \theta, 5 \theta$. As we know that,
$\angle A+\angle B+\angle C=180^{{}^{\circ}}\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & 3 \theta+4 \theta+5 \theta=180^{{}^{\circ}} \\ \Rightarrow & 12 \theta=180^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow \theta=15^{{}^{\circ}}\end{array}
So, angle are 45^{{}^{\circ}}, 60^{{}^{\circ}}, 75^{{}^{\circ}}$.
Now, $\sin A=\sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin$ B=\sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}=$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin$ C=\sin 75^{{}^{\circ}}=$\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2 \sqrt{2}}
So, $\quad a: b: c=\sin A: \sin B: \sin $ C\begin{aligned}$&=$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$: $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$: $\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$\\
&=2: $\sqrt{6}$: $\sqrt{3}+1
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a $\triangle A B C$ if $b=2, B=30^{{}^{\circ}}$ then the area of the circumcircle of $\triangle A B C$ in square units is
questions.solution: We have, $\frac{b}{\sin B}=$2 R $\Rightarrow \quad R=\frac{B}{2 \sin B}=\frac{2}{2 \times \sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}}=2\therefore$ Area of circumcircle $=\pi R^{2}=\pi(2)^{2}=4 \pi$

questions.q: If $\frac{b+c}{11}=\frac{c+a}{12}=\frac{a+b}{13}$, then $\cos A$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $\frac{b+c}{11}=\frac{c+a}{12}=\frac{a+b}{13}=k\Rightarrow b+c=11 k, c+a=12 k, a+b=13 k$
Now, $2(a+b+c)=36 ka+b+c=18 k$
So, $a=7 kb=6 k$
and $\quad c=5 k$
Now, $\quad \cos A=\frac{b^{2}+c^{2}-a^{2}}{2 b c}$
=$\frac{36 k^{2}+25 k^{2}-49 k^{2}}{2\left(30 k^{2}\right)}=\frac{12 k^{2}}{60 k^{2}}=\frac{1}{5}$
